title: Protocol
description: Every frame in both directions, as one schema root (for generating client types).

AppRelease.description: A build of the phone app, offered as an update.

notes.description: What's new, a line or a few.

sha256.description: The APK's SHA-256, hex, to check the download.

version_code.description: Android's version number: higher is newer.

BlockedPcInfo.description: A PC blocked from asking to join.

at.description: When it was blocked, Unix ms.

oneOf.description: The terminal app.
A browser.
The desktop app.
The Android app.
Telegram.
Scripts (`thrall run`).
A companion PC's runner (`thrall runner`), doing that PC's share of the work.

skill.description:
It's a skill or a built-in Thrall carries out itself (`/humanise`): clients send
`/name …` as a message, and Thrall does it.

DeviceInfo.description: A browser or PC signed in as a person.

added.description: When it signed in, Unix ms.

last_seen.description: When it last connected, Unix ms.

name.description: The name it signed in under.

path.description: File path as shown to the user.

DiffKind.description: What a diff does to its file.

oneOf.description: New file.
Changed file.
Removed file.

edition.description: `home` (free, for a household). Other editions may come later.

model.description: The model turns use now (`status` events report changes).

version.description: Engine version; a client built for another version may offer to restart the engine.

oneOf.description: Bad or missing token.
Unknown request type or protocol version.
Malformed request.
Session, turn, request or file doesn't exist.
Can't do that while a turn is running.
Someone else answered that prompt first.
No such slash command.
Too many requests.
The AI provider failed or timed out.
No AI key set.
The AI provider didn't accept the key.
The AI provider refused the request (unknown model, too long, out of credit, …).
Frame or file over the limit.
Engine bug.

EventFrame.description: One frame the engine sends about a session: the envelope fields plus the event itself.

seq.description:
Position in the session's event log. Absent on live-only events (deltas), which are never
stored: after a reconnect the client gets the matching `message.completed` instead.

oneOf.description: A turn began.

scheduled.description:
Nobody started it: a scheduled job or a check-in (clients don't announce it as the
person's own work finishing).

oneOf.description: A turn ended.

A turn was taken back, with every turn after it (the person edited or retried their last
message, or rewound): clients remove what it and the later turns showed.
A message began (Thrall's reply, or an echo of the user's message for other clients).
More text for a message being written. Live-only.
More thinking text, for models that expose it. Live-only.
A message is finished; `text` is the full final text.

text.description: Full text; clients replace what they streamed with this.

oneOf.description: A tool call began (a collapsible row in clients).

helper.description:
The helper's own step when a helper took this step: clients list it under that one.
Several helpers can run at once, so their steps interleave.

oneOf.description: Live output from a running step (shell). Live-only; capped.
A tool call finished.

files.description: Files the step made (pictures), fetched with `GET /v1/files/{file}`.

saved.description:
Files the step wrote on the computer (a saved document, a picture's copy, a download):
the desktop app opens them with `step.file.open`, other clients fetch them with
`step.file.read`, both by their place in this list.

oneOf.description: The session's task list changed (the whole list each time).
Thrall wants permission before doing something.

diff.description: The change, for file edits (accept is `yes`, reject is `no`).

step.description: The step waiting on the answer.

oneOf.description: In plan mode, Thrall presents a plan and waits for a decision.
A plan was approved or turned down.

Thrall needs information it can't safely guess (not permission). One card holds every
question of the turn, each with Thrall's recommended answer picked. Nobody answering by
`expires_at` means the recommended answers are used.

expires_at.description: When Thrall goes ahead with its recommended answers, Unix ms.

why.description: Why Thrall is asking instead of deciding, in a sentence.

oneOf.description: A question card was answered, or ran out of time.

answered_by.description: Which client answered; `timeout` when nobody did and the recommended answers were used.

answers.description: One answer per question, in order.

oneOf.description: A permission request was answered.
Session details changed.

mode_limit.description: How long Full auto lasts (sent with `mode: full_auto`).

workspace.description: New folder the session works in.

oneOf.description: A background helper (or scheduled job) started.
A background helper (or scheduled job) finished.

What the session is doing, and the model in use; sent whenever either changes. Live-only:
`session.opened` carries the current state for a client that (re)attaches.

state.description: Idle, working, or waiting for an answer.

oneOf.description:
Thrall saved a lasting fact about the person to long-term memory. Clients show it with a
way to forget it (`memory.forget`).
Something worth telling the user that isn't a question.

The owner asked for the newest version (`update.install`): the desktop app installs it.
Sent only to the owner's desktop app, with an empty `session`.

Open a file a step wrote, or show it in its folder (`step.file.open`): the desktop app does
it. Sent only to that person's desktop app on this computer, with an empty `session`.

reveal.description: Show it in its folder instead of opening it.

oneOf.description:
The PCs asking to join changed (one asked, or its request ended): ask `pc.requests` for
the list. Sent only to the owner's clients on this computer, with an empty `session`.

Work for a companion PC's runner (sent only to its link, with an empty `session`): run
`job` (`{"phase": "check" | "run" | "stop" | "read" | "write", ...}`) in `workspace` for
`person`'s `in_session`, and answer with `runner.done {call}`.
Something failed.

message.description: Plain-language explanation and what to do.

at.description: When it was saved, Unix ms.

FileRef.description: A file attached to a message. Clients fetch it with `GET /v1/files/{file}`.

kind.description: `image` · `document` · `text` · `other`, so clients know how to show it.

FolderEntry.description: One entry in a folder listing.

GroupInfo.description: One of the person's session groups.

HelperTypeInfo.description: A helper type, for the settings screen.

model.description: Its own model, if it has one.

read_only.description: It only looks (works in plan mode).

KeyStatus.description: Whether a key is stored (`thrall key set <name>`). Never the key itself.

LessonInfo.description: A lesson in the experience log, for the settings screen.

at.description: When it was noted, Unix ms.

LocalFound.description: A program or model server found on this computer, for one of Thrall's jobs.

models.description: Model ids to pick for the job, as Thrall takes them (`program/whisper/ggml-base.en`).

note.description: What it has, or what's missing and how to add it.

ready.description: It can do the job now (installed, running, with a model).

ModeLimit.description: How long Full auto lasts in a session.

ends_at.description: When it goes back to Ask, Unix milliseconds (`time` only).

until.description:
`task_end` (back to Ask when the task finishes) · `time` (back to Ask at `ends_at`) ·
`manual` (until switched off, or Thrall restarts).

oneOf.description: For information.
Worth attention.

OverseenChat.description: One of someone's chats, as the owner sees it with oversight.

flagged.description: Why it was flagged (something wasn't allowed), if it was.

readable.description: The owner can read it at this level.

updated.description: When it was last active, Unix ms.

name.description: This computer's name, as companions see it.

port.description: Its port, on every network this computer is on.

PcRequestInfo.description: A PC asking to join as someone's companion.

address.description: Where it's asking from (its network address).

code.description: The code both screens show: if they match, nobody is in between.

name.description: The name the PC gave (its computer name).

PermissionChoice.description: An answer to a permission request.

oneOf.description: Go ahead, once.
Don't.
Go ahead, and don't ask again for this kind of action.

PersonInfo.description: A person who uses this Thrall.

added.description: When they were added, Unix ms.

key_set.description: Their own AI key is set (it's never shown).

model.description: Their own model, if they have one.

monthly_limit.description: Their monthly spending limit in US dollars, if they have one.

own_key.description: Their turns use their own AI key.

phones.description: How many phones are paired to them.

rules.description: What the owner allows them (everything, unless turned off).

spent.description:
What their turns have cost (USD) since `people.list`'s `since`. Only what was recorded
with a price counts.

PersonRules.description:
What the owner allows a person. Everything is allowed until the owner turns it off; the
person can see what's off for them.

child.description: A child's account, with answers fit for their age: `under_13`, `13_15` or `16_17`.

no_commands.description: Thrall can't run commands for them (the shell and git).

no_system_folders.description:
Thrall's file tools keep out of the system's folders (Windows, programs, other people's
folders) for them.

oversight.description:
What the owner can see of their chats: `summary` (titles and when), `flagged` (that, and
the chats where something wasn't allowed) or `full` (every chat). They're always told.

PersonalityPreset.description: A personality preset, for the settings screen.

added.description: When it was paired, Unix ms.

last_seen.description: When it last connected, Unix ms (absent if never since pairing).

name.description: The name it gave when pairing.

person.description: Whose phone it is (a person's id).

options.description: Answers to pick from (the person can always type their own instead).

recommended.description: Thrall's recommended answer: picked to start with, and used if nobody answers.

address.description: The public address phones use (`remote.address`; "" when not set).

port.description: Its port on 127.0.0.1 (what the tunnel forwards to).

ReplyFrame.description: One frame the engine sends in answer to a request.

oneOf.description: Answer to `hello`.

capabilities.description: Features this engine has, so clients don't guess.

protocol.description: The protocol major both sides will speak.

Answer to `home.get` and `home.clear`.
Answer to `heartbeat.get` and `heartbeat.set`.

checklist.description: The checklist ("" when there isn't one).

next_run.description: When the next check-in is due, Unix ms (absent while check-ins are off).

oneOf.description: Answer to personality.get and personality.set.

custom.description: Your own words (kept even while a preset is chosen).

preset.description: The chosen preset's id, or custom.

presets.description: The presets on offer, standard first.

oneOf.description: Answer to startup.get and startup.set.

available.description: This system can start Thrall at sign-in (the desktop app is installed beside the engine).

label.description:
What the setting is called on the engine's system ("Start with Windows", "Open at
login", "Start when I log in"); empty from an older engine.

oneOf.description: Answer to `folders.get`.

data.description: The data folder: settings, the database, logs (`%APPDATA%\Thrall` on Windows).

work.description:
Thrall's working folder, where Home and new folders go (`Documents\Thrall`), if this
computer has one.

oneOf.description: Answer to `command.list`.
Answer to `command.run`.
What a recording says (answers `audio.transcribe`).
Answer to `checkpoint.preview`.

files.description: The files a rewind would put back, in the order they were first changed.

text.description: What the user typed to start it (their messages in it, joined).

oneOf.description: Answer to `turn.rewind`.

failed.description: Files that couldn't be put back, each with the reason.

restored.description: Files put back (or removed, if the turn made them).

text.description: What the user typed to start the turn, to put back in the message box.

oneOf.description: Answer to `experience.list` and `experience.forget`.
Answer to `skill.get` and `skill.edit`.
Answer to `skill.make_safe`: a safer version, not saved.

rating.description: What this version would be rated: `low`, `medium` or `high`.

oneOf.description: Answer to `memory.list`.
Answer to `settings.get`.

config.description:
`config.toml` as JSON, with values that could be secrets (MCP server environment
variables that aren't keychain references) replaced by `"••••"`.

config_file.description: Where the file is, if the engine has a data folder.

helper_types.description: Helper types Thrall can hand work to: its own and the person's (`agents/<name>.md`).

keys.description: Keys Thrall knows about and whether each is stored.

mcp_signed_in.description: MCP servers on the web that Thrall is signed in to (`/mcp login <name>`).

model.description: The model turns use now (`/model` can differ from the file until restart).

pending.description: Saved settings not in use yet: they apply when Thrall finishes what it's doing.

plan_models.description: Chat models the person's ChatGPT plan offers (`chatgpt/<model>`), when signed in.

skills.description:
Skills Thrall can use (in the session folder `settings.get` was asked about, or only
the person's own), including ones turned off.

oneOf.description: Answer to `local.find`.

items.description: What was found, and what wasn't, job by job.

models_dir.description:
The folder local models go in (whisper.cpp models in `whisper/`, Piper voices in
`piper/`), when Thrall has a data folder.

oneOf.description: Answer to `provider.test`.

message.description: What happened, in plain words (credit left, or what's wrong and how to fix it).

models.description:
Models it offers, as Thrall names them (`direct/openai/gpt-5`, `local/llama3.1`), when
it lists them.

ok.description: It answered and took the key.

oneOf.description: Answer to `phone.list` and `phone.remove`.
Answer to `people.chats`.

items.description: Their chats, most recently active first.

Answer to `pc.requests`, `pc.accept`, `pc.decline` and `pc.unblock`.

items.description: PCs asking to join now, oldest first.

The pairing link the QR holds (`thrall://pair?…`); it contains a secret, so it's shown
only on this computer.

qr.description: The QR code's rows, top to bottom: `1` dark, `0` light (no quiet zone).

oneOf.description: Answer to the `people.*` requests.

items.description: Everyone, the owner first, then oldest first.

code.description: The one-time code (it signs someone in: show it only to them).

expires.description: When it stops working, Unix ms.

oneOf.description: Answer to `device.list` and `device.remove`.

items.description: Signed-in browsers and PCs, newest first.

file.description: Its id, for `turn.send {files}` and further pieces.

name.description: The name it was saved under.

oneOf.description: Answer to `folder.places`.

default.description: Thrall's own folder for sessions started without one picked (`Documents\Thrall`).

new_in.description: Where a new folder goes unless another is picked (`folders.new_in`, else `default`).

recent.description: Folders sessions use, most recently active first.

Answer to `app.latest`.

release.description: The phone app this engine holds; absent when it holds none.

oneOf.description: Answer to `folder.list`.

items.description: Folders first, then files, each newest first.

more.description: Some entries were left out (a very full folder).

path.description: The folder, relative to the session's folder ("" for the folder itself).

Answer to `folder.read` and `step.file.read`: one piece of a file in a session's folder,
or of a file a step wrote.

path.description: The file, relative to the session's folder (for `step.file.read`, its name).

size.description: The whole file's size; the last piece ends there.

oneOf.description: Answer to `file.get`: one piece of a file.

size.description: The whole file's size; the last piece ends there.

id.description: Request id, unique per connection; the reply quotes it as `re`.

oneOf.description: First frame on every connection. Answered by `welcome`.

token.description: Access token (local mode: read from the data folder).

oneOf.description: Heartbeat. Answered by `pong`.
Start a session. Answered by `session.opened`.

title.description: Title (Thrall names it after the first turn otherwise).

oneOf.description:
Attach to a session: `session.opened`, then every stored event after `after_seq` (all of
them when absent), then live events.
Stop receiving a session's events; it keeps running. Answered by `ack`.
Sessions, newest first. Answered by `session.listed`.

archived.description: List archived sessions instead (most recently archived first).

oneOf.description: Archive a session (hidden from the list, kept in full) or bring it back. Answered by `ack`.

archived.description: True to archive, false to bring it back.

oneOf.description: Rename a session. Answered by `ack`; attached clients get `session.updated`.
Change the permission mode. Answered by `ack`; attached clients get `session.updated`.

until.description:
For `full_auto` only, how long it lasts: `task_end` (the default: back to Ask when the
task finishes) · `time` (after `minutes`) · `manual` (until switched off). Full auto
never lasts past a restart of Thrall.

oneOf.description: Pin a session to the top of the list, or unpin it. Answered by `ack`.

Put a session in one of the person's groups, or take it out (no `group`). Answered by
`ack`.

group.description: Group id; absent to take it out of its group.

oneOf.description:
Move a session to another working folder (one that exists). Answered by `ack`; attached
clients get `session.updated`. Refused for Home and while Thrall is working in it.
The person's session groups, in order. Answered by `group.listed`.
Add a group at the end. Answered by `group.listed`.
Rename a group. Answered by `group.listed`.
Delete a group; its sessions stay, ungrouped. Answered by `group.listed`.
Put the groups in this order. Answered by `group.listed`.
Delete a session and its history. Clients ask the user first. Answered by `ack`.

Home, Thrall's built-in conversation: its current page (a fresh one starts when the last
has had its day, per `home.fresh_start`) and earlier pages. Open the page with
`session.open` like any session. Answered by `home.shown`.

Delete every Home page (refused while Thrall is working in Home). Clients ask the person
first. Answered by `home.shown` with a fresh page.
The check-in checklist and when the next check-in is due. Answered by `heartbeat.shown`.

Replace the check-in checklist (empty removes it, which stops check-ins). Answered by
`heartbeat.shown`.

Check in now, whatever the hours. Answered by `ack` at once (or `error {invalid}` with no
checklist); a message in Home follows if something needs the person, else a notice.

Whether Thrall starts when the person signs in to Windows (the same entry as the desktop
app's tray menu). Answered by `startup.shown`.

Start Thrall at sign-in, or stop. Answered by `startup.shown` (or `error {invalid}` where
it isn't available).

Install the newest version of Thrall: the desktop app on the engine's computer checks,
downloads and installs it, and Thrall restarts. Answered by `ack` once the desktop app has
been asked (or `error {invalid}` when it isn't running).
Where Thrall keeps its things on the engine's computer. Answered by `folders.shown`.

Open one of Thrall's folders in the file manager on the engine's computer (the working
folder is made first if it isn't there yet). Answered by `ack`.
Your personality: how Thrall talks to you. Answered by personality.shown.
Choose your personality (only ever your own). Answered by personality.shown.

custom.description: Your own words, used with custom.

preset.description: A preset's id from personality.shown, or custom.

oneOf.description:
Send a message. Answered by ck; the turn's events follow. While a turn is running the
text joins it at its next step instead.

files.description: Ids of files uploaded with `POST /v1/files` to attach.

text.description: What the user typed (`@path` mentions included).

oneOf.description:
What rewinding to before a turn would do: the message that started it and the files to put
back. Answered by `checkpoint.shown`.

turn.description: The turn to go back to before.

oneOf.description:
Go back to before a turn: its files and every later turn's go back to how they were
(`files`), and/or the turn and every later one is taken back (`conversation`, one
`turn.retracted` for `turn`). Refused while a turn runs. Answered by `turn.rewound`.

keep.description: Files (as `checkpoint.shown` names them) to leave as they are.

turn.description: The turn to go back to before.

oneOf.description:
Run the last message again: its turn is taken back (`turn.retracted`), the files it changed
go back to how they were (except ones changed since by someone else, which a notice
names) and the same text is sent as a new turn. Refused while a turn runs. Answered by
`ack`.

Replace the last message: its turn is taken back (files too, as for `turn.retry`) and
`text` sent instead. Refused while a turn runs. Answered by `ack`.
Stop the running turn (Esc). Answered by `ack`.
Answer a `permission.request`. Answered by `ack`, or `error {already_answered}`.
Approve or turn down a `plan.proposed`. Answered by `ack`, or `error {already_answered}`.

auto_edits.description: Approve and let file edits go ahead without asking.

oneOf.description:
Answer a `question.ask`: one answer per question, in order. Answered by `ack`, or
`error {already_answered}`.

Receive events from every session, not only the ones opened (the desktop app uses this for
its tray icon and notifications). Live text (deltas, output) is left out. Answered by `ack`.

Stop the engine (the desktop app's Quit, when the person chooses to stop it too). Answered
by `ack`; then every connection closes.

Turn an uploaded recording (`POST /v1/files`) into text: the app's microphone button.
Answered by `audio.transcribed`.

session.description: Session the cost belongs to, if any.

oneOf.description: The slash commands, for autocomplete. Answered by `command.listed`.
Run a slash command. Answered by `command.result`.

session.description: Session it applies to, if any.

oneOf.description: The lessons in your experience log, newest first. Answered by `experience.listed`.
Delete a lesson from your experience log. Answered by `experience.listed`.
The facts Thrall remembers about the person, newest first. Answered by `memory.listed`.
Forget a fact: it's no longer recalled. Answered by `ack`, or `error {not_found}`.

Remove one of the person's own skills (its folder is deleted). Project skills can only be
turned off. Answered by `settings.shown`.

One of the person's own skills in full, to read or edit. Answered by `skill.shown`, or
`error {invalid}` when there's no such skill of theirs.

Change one of the person's own skills. A skill Thrall learned is rated again from what it
now says (the person wrote it, so only what it does can raise the rating). Answered by
`skill.shown`, or `error {invalid}` with the reason.

description.description: When to use it, one sentence.

oneOf.description:
Ask the model for a safer version of one of the person's own skills: the same job without
deleting, sending, handling keys or running downloads on its own (it asks the person
instead). Nothing is saved: `skill.edit` with the answer keeps it. Answered by
`skill.safer`, or `error {invalid}` / `error {provider_unavailable}`.

The engine's settings, for the settings screen (read only for now). Key values never
leave the engine: only whether each one is set. Answered by `settings.shown`.

Change one setting in `config.toml` (comments kept). Used at once when Thrall is idle,
otherwise when its work finishes (`pending` in the answer). Answered by `settings.shown`,
or `error {invalid}` with the reason (unknown setting, wrong type).

Check that a supplier works with the key Thrall has for it (the key never leaves the
engine), and list the models it offers. The owner only. Answered by `provider.tested`.

Look on this computer for programs and model servers that can do Thrall's jobs (Ollama,
LM Studio, whisper.cpp, Piper, a Stable Diffusion web UI). Nothing is installed or
downloaded. The owner only. Answered by `local.found`.

Paired phones and the phone link's state. Not on the phone link itself. Answered by
`phone.listed`.

Start pairing a phone: a one-time code shown as a QR. Needs `remote.address`. Not on the
phone link itself. Answered by `phone.pairing`.

person.description: Who the phone is for (a person's id); absent: the owner.

oneOf.description:
Give a paired phone to another person: it reconnects as them. Not on the phone link
itself. Answered by `phone.listed`.

Forget a phone: it can't connect again, and its open connection closes. Not on the phone
link itself. Answered by `phone.listed`.

PCs asking to join as someone's companion, and the PCs blocked from asking. The owner
only, not over a link. Answered by `pc.requests`.

Let a PC that's asking join, as `person`'s. `code`, when given, must be the code the PC
shows (typed instead of compared by eye). Answered by `pc.requests`.

code.description: The code the PC shows, typed by the owner.

person.description: Whose PC it is (a person's id).

oneOf.description: Turn a PC that's asking away; with `block`, it can't ask again. Answered by `pc.requests`.

A companion PC's runner is ready: from now on this link gets `runner.call` events for the
sessions that work on this PC. Only on a joined PC's link. Answered by `ack`.

home.description: The PC's Thrall folder (where its sessions work unless one picks another).

oneOf.description: Live output of a call the runner is running (a command's lines). Answered by `ack`.
What came of a call. Answered by `ack`.

error.description: Why it didn't, when it didn't.

oneOf.description:
Set what a person is allowed (the owner only; not the owner's own). Answered by
`people.listed`.

Someone's chats, as far as their oversight lets the owner see them (owner only). Answered
by `people.chats`.

Read one of someone's chats (owner only; `full`, or `flagged` and the chat was). Answered by
`people.chat`. The view is noted in the audit log.
Let a blocked PC ask again. Answered by `pc.requests`.

The people who use this Thrall (anyone but the owner: only themselves). Answered by
`people.listed`.

since.description:
Count each person's spending from this moment (Unix ms), e.g. the start of this month
where the asker is; absent: all of it.

oneOf.description: Add a person (a member). Owner only. Answered by `people.listed`.
Rename a person. Owner only. Answered by `people.listed`.
Set what a person's turns run on and may spend. Owner only. Answered by `people.listed`.

model.description: Their own model; absent: the engine's. Not for the owner (who changes the engine's).

monthly_limit.description: The most their turns may cost in a calendar month, in US dollars; absent: no limit.

own_key.description: Their turns use their own AI key (not the owner's). Not for the owner.

oneOf.description:
Keep (or, without `key`, forget) a person's own AI key. Yours, or (the owner) anyone's;
never shown back. The owner's own key is set with `thrall key set`. Answered by `ack`.

key.description: The key; absent or empty: forget it.

oneOf.description:
Remove a person: they can't connect any more and their phones are forgotten; their
sessions and files are kept. The owner can't be removed. Owner only. Answered by

A one-time sign-in link for a person: the browser that opens it signs in as them. Owner
